Key participants: Fredrik Jørgensen (customer, Oda), Christian Liebenow (GrowthBook sales rep). Product: GrowthBook (experimentation platform, self-hosted enterprise version). calls.title: Oda + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The meeting detailed a tailored enterprise proposal from GrowthBook to ODA, proposing an annual platform fee starting at $100,000, with a discount of $50,000 due to budget limitations. User fees were established at $1,250 for authorized users and $500 for read-only users. A commitment to a case study could yield an additional discount, pending satisfactory outcomes. ODA's CTO’s budget constraints were a significant hurdle for acceptance. Additionally, GrowthBook highlighted key product features, including self-hosting capabilities and robust support models, while confirming ODA's preference for experimentation features, leading to a proposed partnership aimed for conclusion by April 30.

calls.title: Oda & GrowthBook Case Study
calls.summary: The team detailed their significant advancements in embedding experimentation into product development, emphasizing the use of Growth Book for running approximately 50 active experiments since 2021. They highlighted the benefits of A/B testing and control rollouts in validating features that positively impact profitability. The strategic approach prioritizes learning and risk mitigation, with concrete case studies demonstrating impressive outcomes, such as a 16-17% growth in usage through personalization improvements. Their technology stack, including Snowflake and Looker, is designed for flexibility and deep data integration, enhancing their experimentation process. Looking ahead, they plan to leverage new features from Growth Book to accelerate experimentation cycles and foster a culture of continuous learning.
calls.keywords: GrowthBook, experimentation, Bayesian statistics, product personalization, A/B testing, data analytics

calls.title: Medcof + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The team is transitioning from using GrowthBook primarily for feature flags to incorporating experimentation, aimed at gathering richer user data to enhance understanding of user behavior. Currently, GrowthBook has seen limited A/B testing, and the lack of sufficient user data is a driving force for this shift. Product managers are actively exploring experimental setups, with demonstrations on tracking metrics and validating experiment traffic. As of now, usage of GrowthBook has exceeded its set limits, prompting plans to upgrade to an Enterprise plan to accommodate growth. Integration with Google Analytics is anticipated to simplify metric setup, while discussions around advanced metrics indicate a user-defined approach. AI-powered tools are expected to enhance experimentation and metric management, alongside addressing security concerns related to feature flagging in production environments.
calls.keywords: experiment setup, feature flags, data pipelines, Google Analytics integration, AI assistant, product analytics

calls.title: Demo Call with Ashley Gates from Cleo
calls.summary: The meeting addressed Clio's lack of a formal feature flagging system, with the team seeking a solution that simplifies integration for product managers. Ashley highlighted the current reliance on manual processes involving developers and support engineers, indicating a need for a centralized system. Concerns arose regarding their technical constraints, particularly the absence of a data warehouse. GrowthBook was introduced as a potential solution offering a managed cloud platform that supports over 25 SDK languages and provides features tailored for product managers. The conversation also touched on the importance of flexible feature flagging in relation to AI-driven product development, current rollout strategies, and ongoing technical considerations. The team agreed to schedule a follow-up demo for further exploration of integration details.
calls.keywords: feature flagging, AI-driven deployment, GrowthBook demo, multi-tenant targeting, managed vs self-hosted, lambda cold start latency

calls.title: Matthew Rosebrook and Ashley Stirrup
calls.summary: The discussion focused on the potential acquisition of the domain name release.com, which has an initial price set at $2 million with a $500k minimum bid. Matt highlighted the owner's expectations and exclusivity conditions, while Ashley expressed uncertainty about the domain's value given her company's current business focus. Despite the domain's broad market interest, particularly from AI-related companies, its direct fit with Ashley's marketing needs was questioned. The parties acknowledged the premium pricing and market trends, with a plan for Ashley to consult her CEO regarding potential bids, while Matt will confirm pricing information to facilitate future negotiations.
calls.keywords: domain acquisition, release.com, feature flags, rebranding, AI transition, pricing negotiation
